messages:
alex: Customer reported recurring 429s during short bursts this morning. They’re on our hosted API, using an API key tied to a project with plenty of quota. They also send requests through a third-party proxy that NATs to a small set of egress IPs. Behavior: ~30s spike -> lots of 429s, then clears. Customer insists their key is fine. Asking for help to confirm scoping logic and quick mitigation.

maya: Can you paste a sample request/headers and the 429 response headers? Also which timestamps so we can pull logs.

alex: Here's the header snippet customer provided (redacted key):

```\nPOST /v1/generate\nHost: api.redwood.ai\nAuthorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTED\nX-Forwarded-For: 52.12.34.56\nUser-Agent: customer-app/1.2.3\n```

And the 429 body they saw: `{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","retry_after":3}`. They also forwarded our 429 response headers: `X-RateLimit-Scope: ip`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`.

Time window: first seen 1769989920, last spike finished ~1769990300.

sam: Interesting — header shows our rate limiter attributed to IP (nat) instead of API key. Our intended precedence is: API key > project > org > IP as fallback. If the key is present we should attribute to that.

jordan: Customer says some requests have no Authorization header because their proxy strips it for certain endpoints and re-injects a rotated token at the proxy layer. Could be intermittent header removal + NAT causing the same IP to hit quota.

maya: Can you grep the auth attribution logs for that time window? We log attribution as `auth_id=<type>:<id>` at request accept time. If it says `ip:52.12.34.56` we'll confirm. If it says `key:proj-123` then rate limit should be key-scoped.

alex: Pulled a few lines from ingress logs (sanitized):

```\n1769989952 INFO request id=xyz auth_id=ip:52.12.34.56 route=/v1/generate latency=45ms status=429\n1769989954 INFO request id=abc auth_id=key:proj-123 route=/v1/generate latency=38ms status=200\n1769990010 INFO request id=def auth_id=ip:52.12.34.56 route=/v1/generate latency=40ms status=429\n```

So we have interleaving — same client surface showing both key and ip attribution. That would explain 429s when proxy strips header on some calls.

sam: That matches. Two notes: 1) If header absent we attribute to NAT IP. 2) We also have a heuristic that if X-Forwarded-For exists we prioritize IP attribution for certain internal CIDR ranges to defend against credential spoofing. Maybe that heuristic is too aggressive and is catching this proxy.

maya: Rolling repro suggestion: customer to run a short script that alternates requests with and without Authorization to confirm behavior. Example repro: 

```bash\n# run from customer environment (with/without auth)\nfor i in {1..60}; do\n  if (( i % 2 == 0 )); then\n    curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTED" -H "X-Forwarded-For: 52.12.34.56" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate\n  else\n    curl -s -H "X-Forwarded-For: 52.12.34.56" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate\n  fi\ndone\n```

Expect: alternating 200 and 429 when IP quota hits.

alex: Customer ran it and attached results: they saw 8 consecutive 429s after about 22s. They also captured which requests had Authorization present — the proxy sometimes fails to include it on retry.

maya: Short-term mitigation options we can suggest to the customer: 1) Ensure proxy preserves Authorization header or replays the same key consistently. 2) Ask them to use a dedicated egress IP (if using managed proxy) so quota mapping is clearer. 3) We can temporarily raise their project quota to absorb burst while they fix proxy behavior. Which do they prefer?

jordan: They asked for a quick server-side change so they don't need to change proxy right away. Can we change attribution precedence to prefer API key if present even when X-Forwarded-For is set?

sam: We should be careful — we put the X-Forwarded-For prioritization because some customers were forging Authorization to escalate. But we can change the order to: 1) validated API key token (checked via signature lookup) 2) project/org fallback 3) ip attribution. If Authorization header is present and validates to an existing key we should always prefer it. That seems safe.

maya: Operational action: open an internal ticket to patch auth attribution ordering. Also add a temporary flag to routing to prefer key when present for this customer only (config override) as an emergency mitigant. I'll own the SRE side.

alex: I'll propose the temporary quota bump and ask the customer to enable header passthrough. Jordan, can you confirm if they'd accept quota bump?

jordan: Yes they asked for the bump and the temporary config change. They’ll also aim to fix proxy by EOD.

rate-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1182 - "auth attribution: aggressive ip precedence leads to burst 429s". Assigned to maya. Priority: P2.

maya: Next steps: 1) Patch attribution ordering in routing (small PR), 2) Apply per-customer override to prefer key for proj-123, 3) Apply temporary quota bump + monitor, 4) Postmortem + doc updates about proxies and header preservation.

alex: I'll message the customer with mitigation steps and request their go-ahead. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

sam: For follow-up engineering note — add unit tests for mixed-auth stream where Authorization toggles mid-session; ensure KV cache and rate limiter see consistent auth mapping for retries.

jordan: I'll attach the customer's repro logs to the ticket and confirm when proxy fix is deployed.

maya: Closing loop here after we confirm patch and bump.
